clue.text: Jack the mackerel catcher

definitions.meaning: Jack of the nursery rhyme who could eat no fat
the proverb speaks of risking a small fish to catch a mackerel

explanation.surface: A fisherman called Jack who lands mackerel.
explanation.walkthrough: Two senses: Jack Sprat of the English nursery rhyme, and the small fish in the saying 'a sprat to catch a mackerel', a small outlay risked for a large gain.
explanation.definitionFit: The nursery-rhyme Jack shares his surname with the small bait fish of the proverb.

clue.text: Officer makes naval vessel change direction

parts.note: sub is short for submarine
to change is to alter
N stands for north, a compass direction

explanation.surface: An officer has a warship turn about.
explanation.definitionFit: A subaltern is a junior army officer below captain.

clue.text: Numerical comparison shows a trio's right at the top

indicators.note: at the top means the letter for right is shifted to the front of the word

parts.note: taken as written, the possessive adding no letter

explanation.surface: Statistics show a threesome are correct at the top.
explanation.walkthrough: In A TRIO the R (right) moves to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratio expresses the relative size of two quantities.

clue.text: In West End, foreign money can be a bother

indicators.note: the end of the word West is its final letter

parts.note: the rouble is the Russian currency

explanation.surface: Foreign cash causing problems in London's theatre district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West End' looks like London's theatreland, but 'End' just takes the last letter of West.
explanation.definitionFit: Trouble is difficulty or nuisance.

clue.text: Pope succeeds in being far from fair

indicators.note: succeeds means comes after, so the papal name follows the little word

parts.note: Clement is the name taken by fourteen popes

explanation.surface: A pontiff who manages to be anything but just.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fair' reads as just, but here it is fair weather; 'being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Inclement weather is stormy and harsh, the very opposite of fine.

clue.text: Insignificant type belonging to religious group

parts.note: belonging to a club is being in it
a sect is a religious group

explanation.surface: A lowly member of a religious order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Insignificant type' looks like part of a description, but it defines the answer, used of a contemptible person.
explanation.definitionFit: A person regarded as small and worthless is called a bug or creepy-crawly.

clue.text: Upset when measured for top team award?

parts.note: a cap is awarded to a player selected for a national team
measured for a fitting is sized

explanation.surface: A player is upset while being fitted for an international cap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' reads as distressed, but it means overturned, as a boat; 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A capsized boat has been overturned.

clue.text: These novel diamonds may be cut with ease

indicators.note: may be signals that the letters of the two words can become something else

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Gems that a cutter could shape easily.
explanation.walkthrough: The Eustace Diamonds is a novel by Anthony Trollope; 'cut' suggests gem-cutting but it is anagram fodder with 'ease'.
explanation.definitionFit: Trollope's novel is titled The Eustace Diamonds, so the name identifies those jewels.

clue.text: Very active in one quarter, erecting new construction

parts.note: E for east is one quarter of the compass

indicators.note: a new construction of the letters means they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A busy builder putting up something new in one part of town.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone energetic is lively and full of vigour.

clue.text: Rebel US President

definitions.meaning: Wat ... led the Peasants' Revolt of 1381 in England
John ... was the tenth President of the United States

explanation.surface: An American president who went against his party.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the leader of the English Peasants' Revolt and the tenth American president bore this surname.

clue.text: Encouragement to finish drinking 5

definitions.meaning: a toast urging everyone to drain their glasses
refers to the answer at 5 down, meaning upset or overturned

explanation.surface: A drinking toast, with a cross-reference.
explanation.walkthrough: The 5 points to 5 down, CAPSIZED: a capsized boat is upside down, keel uppermost.
explanation.definitionFit: The toast tells drinkers to tip glasses upright-to-inverted, and a capsized hull is likewise inverted.

clue.text: Deliver letters in short time

definitions.meaning: to say the letters of a word in order
a brief period, as in a sunny interval

explanation.surface: A postman with only a little time for his round.
explanation.definitionFit: To recite a word letter by letter is one sense; a brief period, such as a cold one, is the other.

clue.text: Turn round and glower on stage?

definitions.text: Turn round and glower on stage?

parts.words: Turn round and glower on stage
parts.note: turning round is glancing behind, glowering is being furious, and on stage points to a theatre title

explanation.surface: An actor told to spin and scowl.
explanation.walkthrough: John Osborne's 1956 play gave the 'angry young men' their name; the clue spells out its title phrase by phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of Osborne's famous drama, read literally, describes a furious glance behind.

clue.text: Part of canine, namely its coating

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A dentist describing what covers a dog tooth.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR text read 'ceiling'; the page prints 'coating'. 'Canine' looks like a dog, but the hidden letters straddle 'canine, namely'.
explanation.definitionFit: The hard white outer layer of a tooth covers it as a protective layer.

clue.text: Keepers of records for Freud and Jung, say

indicators.note: say signals that the following word is spoken and heard as another

parts.note: both were psychoanalysts, analysts for short

explanation.surface: Notes kept by the founders of psychoanalysis.
explanation.definitionFit: Writers of annals chronicle events year by year.

clue.text: Couldn't stand trial, when caught in the act

indicators.note: caught in means the trial word is trapped inside the act word

parts.note: an act or action is a deed
a trial is a test

explanation.surface: A defendant unfit to face court after being caught red-handed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Couldn't stand trial' reads as a legal phrase, but 'Couldn't stand' is the definition and 'trial' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unable to bear something means hating it.

clue.text: Encourage lady, one might infer, to be cleaner

parts.note: deter is the opposite of encourage, as the inference reverses each word
gent is the male counterpart of lady

explanation.surface: Coaxing a woman to be tidier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One might infer' tells you to take the opposites: the opposite of encourage is DETER, of lady GENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A detergent is a cleaning agent.

clue.text: Northern paper, or one of its readers

definitions.meaning: a native of Scotland, who might read that paper

explanation.surface: A Scottish newspaper and its typical subscriber.
explanation.definitionFit: The Edinburgh broadsheet takes its title from the word for a man from Scotland.

clue.text: Mythical paragon?

parts.note: a model of perfection so peerless that no equal exists, as though it were only a legend

explanation.surface: A legendary model of excellence.
explanation.definitionFit: An unrivalled person or thing is one whose like is not found anywhere.

clue.text: Last in race, and second last in high jump?

parts.note: the bar starts low and rises, so the lowest height is the last one cleared in reverse; least high

explanation.surface: Finishing behind everyone and next to bottom in an athletics event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last in high jump' suggests the final, highest attempt, but it means the least high.
explanation.definitionFit: The runner who comes last is the least quick.

clue.text: Gus is a practical example of one

definitions.text: Gus is a practical example of one

parts.words: Gus is a practical example of one
parts.note: Gus the Theatre Cat appears in T. S. Eliot's Old Possum's Book of Practical Cats

explanation.surface: A man named Gus held up as a hands-on model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Practical' looks like ordinary praise, but it points to Eliot's book of Practical Cats, where Gus is the elderly theatre cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Gus is a male cat, and a male domestic feline is so called.

clue.text: In part of Bible, section 5

indicators.note: In puts the section word inside the Bible abbreviation

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament
a verse is a section of a poem or chapter

explanation.surface: A Bible reference to chapter five.
explanation.walkthrough: 5 refers to 5 down, CAPSIZED; overset is an old word for overturned.
explanation.definitionFit: Overset is an archaic term for overturn or upset, like a capsized boat.

clue.text: Equality for one not politically independent

indicators.note: the numeral one is set within the political word as its stand-in

parts.note: someone not independent belongs to a party
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Fair shares for a politician who follows the whip.
explanation.walkthrough: The loose 'for' places I (one) inside PARTY, the opposite of political independence.
explanation.definitionFit: Parity is equal status or value.

clue.text: Line who's left in the same boat, perhaps

definitions.text: Line who's left in the same boat, perhaps

parts.words: Line who's left in the same boat, perhaps
parts.note: left means of left-wing sympathies, and being in the same boat suggests a shared journey

explanation.surface: A castaway still aboard with others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like remaining behind, but it means left-wing: the term is used for a communist sympathiser who is not a party member, and literally for a fellow passenger.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-member who sympathises with communism is so called, as is a companion on a journey.

clue.text: Realize it's a trick

explanation.surface: Seeing that something is a con.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Realize' looks like 'understand', but it means bring in money at sale.
explanation.definitionFit: An item that realizes a sum sells for it; an old sense of the word is a contrivance or ruse.

clue.text: Relaxed game of cards with bridge opponents

parts.note: loo is an old card game
South and East sit as opponents at the bridge table

explanation.surface: A friendly hand of cards against bridge rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: Loo is an old gambling card game; in bridge South and East belong to opposing partnerships.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose means slack or not tight, unconstrained.

clue.text: Sense Simple Simon didn't have

parts.note: in the nursery rhyme, Simple Simon asks the pieman for a sample of his wares but has no penny, so never gets one

explanation.surface: A simpleton lacking common sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sense' suggests common sense, which a simpleton lacks; in the rhyme Simon says 'Let me taste your ware' but is refused without a penny.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the five senses, perceived by the tongue, which Simon never got to use on the pies.

clue.text: Dominates resort in Kent

definitions.note: a place-indicator standing for a town in that county

indicators.note: read as re-sort, meaning sort the letters of the previous word again

explanation.surface: A seaside resort in Kent that rules the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort' looks like a holiday town, but read as re-sort it asks for the letters of 'Dominates' to be rearranged. Kent is a county in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Maidstone is the county town of Kent, so it is a place in that county.

clue.text: No such indecision from Victor?

parts.note: a winner, like Caesar with his veni, vidi, vici, shows no wavering

explanation.surface: A decisive man named Victor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Victor' looks like a name but means a winner, who shows none of the reluctance to act that the answer describes.
explanation.definitionFit: Indecision is a holding back or wavering before acting.

clue.text: Current location for Council of Europe

definitions.meaning: a current here is a flowing river, the third longest in England
the city in northern Italy where the sixteenth-century church council of Catholic Europe met

explanation.surface: Where the Council of Europe sits nowadays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like 'present', but it is a river; the council is the Counter-Reformation Council held in the Italian city of the same name, not the modern Strasbourg body.
explanation.definitionFit: The English river shares its name with the Italian city that hosted the famous sixteenth-century church council.
